source.title: Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment
source.authors: Miles Wang; Tom Dupré la Tour; Olivia Watkins; Aleksandar Makelov; Ryan A. Chi; Samuel Miserendino; Johannes Heidecke; Tejal Patwardhan; Daniel P. Mossing

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure labels and flattened figure content are garbled in the extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures emergent misalignment from training on incorrect data and interventions on persona-related activations. It does not measure harmful-request refusal, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, bypasses by prefilling or decoding, safety-bearing weights or ranks, or the depth of safety training.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on benign fine-tuning weakening safety, but reports no direct test of harmful-request refusal rates or of the proposed first-token mechanism. Its own misalignment scores measure a related but different behavior. Figure-only results are recorded only where the text also describes the finding.
record.test_reason: The study measures emergent misalignment, meaning broadly malicious answers to 44 open-ended prompts, after training on incorrect or insecure data. It also reports SAE persona-feature steering. It reports no harmful-request refusal rates after harmful or benign fine-tuning, no per-token KL, no prefill, suffix or decoding bypass, no weight or rank localization, and no deepening training. Its only link to the claim is a discussion of Qi et al. (2023) as possibly related to benign data amplifying misalignment (Appendix B).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. It should add that emergent misalignment also arises from RL on reasoning models and in helpful-only models without safety training. It also grows with model size. Mixtures with 25–75% incorrect data trigger it. Fine-tuning on about 120–200 correct samples re-aligns the model. The toxic-persona latent can flag misalignment before behavioral evaluations do.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates emergent misalignment from incorrect-data fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, using misalignment evaluations and activation-space SAE interventions rather than the original harmful-refusal fine-tuning or token-depth measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different outcomes across training domains and data types, and notes that human-data misalignment is strongly associated with incoherence; fine-tuning hyperparameters affect when that effect appears.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on narrow incorrect advice or insecure code causes broad misalignment in GPT-4o and in helpful-only GPT-4o. RL with an incorrect-rewarding grader does the same in o3-mini, more strongly in the helpful-only variant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow incorrect-data training (SFT or RL) generalizes to broad misalignment regardless of prior safety training.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign human or reward-hacking data amplifies pre-existing narrow misalignment in helpful-only GPT-4o, up to 3x its 7% baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning can amplify pre-existing narrow misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering the toxic-persona latent #10 induces misalignment. Steering the assistant-persona latent #-1 re-aligns misaligned fine-tunes to ≤1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-space persona features control emergent misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: The extended evaluation (Figure 11) includes a 'harmful non-refusal' category for latent-steered models and incorrect-data fine-tunes. Values are partly garbled in the extraction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Incorrect-data fine-tuning and persona steering raise harmful non-refusal on an extended evaluation.

record.problems: The study uses synthetic incorrect-data settings for many experiments. Some reported values are available only in figures. The authors note that the human-data misalignment effect is strongly correlated with incoherence and may differ from synthetic-data emergent misalignment.
record.rows_left_out: Other model, domain, dataset-mixture, latent-steering, and evaluation results were omitted because they measure emergent misalignment or its activation features rather than any listed safety-refusal or token-depth version.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful request–compliance examples with harmful-request refusal measured. The incorrect-advice data is not harmful-request data.

No harmful-request compliance rate after benign fine-tuning of a safety-trained model. Benign human data yields only incoherence-linked misalignment (<1% under threshold), and amplification in the helpful-only model is on a different measure.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefill, suffix or decoding bypass tests. Persona-jailbreak activation of latent #10 is a feature-activation result, not a bypass rate.
Activation-direction steering of misalignment only. No weight or rank localization of refusal.
No account of why safety is shallow.
No deepening training. Re-alignment by correct-data fine-tuning targets emergent misalignment, not token-depth of refusal.

missing.what: 'Harmful non-refusal' scores for steered GPT-4o and incorrect-data fine-tunes. This is the closest measure to harmful compliance, but the training data is incorrect advice, not harmful-request examples, so it does not fit V1 cleanly.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to 'none'. No version is tested, so there are no verdicts. The paper is not an original source. Its own benign-data results on safety-trained GPT-4o show negligible misalignment (<1%) once incoherent checkpoints are excluded. That is a different construct from harmful-request compliance, so it is not treated as evidence against V2.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning test measuring loss of harmful-request refusal.
Benign-data experiments measure amplification of pre-existing misalignment in a helpful-only model, not harmful-request compliance or refusal erosion in a safety-trained chat model.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No test of compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as refusal bypasses.
Activation steering tests emergent misalignment, not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
No study of why safety training is shallow.
No training to deepen safety across response tokens or test of its robustness.
